correctness.rationale: For element x=sum lambda_v e_v+sum mu_a a the exact multiplication columns are xe_v=lambda_v e_v+sum_{t(a)=v}mu_a a, xa=lambda_{s(a)}a and e_v x=lambda_v e_v+sum_{s(a)=v}mu_a a, ax=lambda_{t(a)}a. Given S of zero lambda values and F nonzero internal E[S] arrows, all arrow columns with sources outside S span sum_{v notin S} d^+(v) coordinate directions; nonzero e_v columns add n-|S| and remaining internal target-supported columns on distinct targets have disjoint supports, giving dim xA=sum_{v notin S}(1+d^+(v))+|T(F)|. Analogous source support gives dim Ax=sum_{v notin S}(1+d^-(v))+|U(F)|. Counting disjoint (S,F) strata gives (q-1)^{n-|S|+|F|}q^{m-|E[S]|} and the boxed bivariate polynomial for every field, loops, parallel arrows. Substituting the three path quivers gives the different rank-one marginals 2(q-1)(q+1), (q-1)(q^2+q+1), (q-1)(q+2); inequalities hold for all q>=2. The sign reversal in commutator coordinate equations under arrow reversal explains a genuine invariant distinction. Independent multiplication-matrix rank enumeration over F_2 and F_3 with loops/parallel arrows corroborates the strata formula; all-quiver conclusion comes from basis linear independence.

originality.rationale: Standard radical-square-zero quiver algebra structure and principal ideal rank interpretation are prior mathematics. Męcel 2016 studies finiteness of conjugacy classes of left ideals over algebraically closed fields, not element-weighted simultaneous left/right ranks over finite fields. Elia–Gorla 2014 algorithm treats individual ranks in group algebras; Lanzilotta et al and Nasr-Isfahani concern homological/singular properties. None of those inspected theorem statements gives the full bivariate quiver polynomial or orientation distinction. The rank calculation is elementary, so a hidden general matrix-support or module enumeration formula is a real priority risk; novelty is only claimed best-of-knowledge.
residual_risks: The closed formula may be implicit in older matrix-support rank distributions or quiver-ideal classification under a different terminology.
An element-weighted polynomial does not count distinct principal ideals or their module isomorphism classes.

value.rationale: The object is standard in representation theory and finite algebra, and the measured invariant is natural: the joint sizes of two principal one-sided ideals generated by a uniformly chosen element. A closed coefficient formula for every finite quiver including loops and multiple arrows is a complete classification of this statistic. It separates all orientations of a three-vertex path despite identical pairwise commuting equations, demonstrating nonredundant algebraic information with exact computable counts.

limitations: Only finite fields, path length-two killed, split basic algebra; arbitrary general finite-dimensional algebra not covered.
